qavajs.config.ts import { defineConfig } from '@qavajs/playwright'; import Memory from './memory'; import App from './page_object'; export default defineConfig({ paths: ['features/*.feature'], require: [ 'node_modules/@qavajs/playwright/steps.js', // package steps 'step_definitions/*.ts' // custom step definitions ], memory: new Memory(), pageObject: new App() }); playwright.config.ts import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test'; export default defineConfig({ testMatch: 'qavajs.config.ts', ... });

Steps log resolved memory values ($url -> https://..., $key <- value) and resolved locators (Form > Button -> locator(...)). Use logger option in qavajs.config.ts to control where logs are written and which values are masked: export default defineConfig({ // ... logger: { output: 'step', // 'console' (default) | 'step' | 'off' mask: /password|token|ssn/i // keys whose values are masked, false disables masking } }); console - logs are printed to stdout (prefixed with worker index when tests run in parallel) step - logs of a step are attached to that step in the report as a single log attachment off - logs are not written Values of memory keys, object properties, query parameters and headers matching mask pattern are replaced with ***. Masked values are remembered and masked wherever they appear later (e.g. interpolated into a url). Default pattern (defaultSecretPattern, exported from @qavajs/playwright) covers password, secret, token, api key, authorization, credential, private key and cookie. Extend it as new RegExp(defaultSecretPattern.source + '|ssn', 'i'). caution Keep secrets in memory rather than in step text: step titles and Playwright action titles are not masked. note Since 4.4.0 step logs are printed to console by default instead of being attached to steps. Set logger.output: 'step' to attach them to the report. note Requires Node.js 22 or later. Only @qavajs/playwright, @qavajs/playwright/steps.js and @qavajs/playwright/lib/electron.js entry points can be imported.

Custom steps are defined with Given/When/Then exported from @qavajs/playwright and can reuse built-in parameter types and world helpers World member Description this.page, this.context, this.browser, this.request Playwright objects of current scenario this.element(path) Resolve page object path to Locator this.value(expression) Resolve memory expression ('$user', '$js(1 + 1)') this.setValue(key, value) Save value to memory this.expect Playwright expect extended with qavajs matchers (see below) this.waitForDialog() Get open dialog or wait for next one this.log(data), this.attach(data, details) Add log or attachment to report import { When, Then, type QavajsPlaywrightWorld, type MemoryValue, type Validation } from '@qavajs/playwright'; import type { Locator } from '@playwright/test'; When('I log in as {value}', async function (this: QavajsPlaywrightWorld, user: MemoryValue) { const { username, password } = await user.value(); await this.element('LoginPage > UsernameInput').fill(username); await this.element('LoginPage > PasswordInput').fill(password); }); Then('I expect placeholder of {locator} {validation} {value}', async function ( this: QavajsPlaywrightWorld, locator: Locator, validation: Validation, expected: MemoryValue ) { // poll retries until validation passes or expect timeout is reached // locator and property are printed in the error message await validation.poll( () => locator.getAttribute('placeholder'), await expected.value(), { locator, property: 'placeholder' } ); }); validation.poll(getter, expected, options?) accepts optional { locator, property, timeout }. The getter receives { timeout } of the current attempt. A polled validation produces a single report step (instead of a step per attempt), and on failure prints the locator, timeout and Playwright call log.

All validations are implemented as Playwright custom matchers, so they produce native Playwright error messages. They are available via this.expect: Matcher Validation toSimpleEqual equal toStrictlyEqual strictly equal toDeepEqual deeply equal toCaseInsensitiveEqual case insensitive equal toInclude contain toMatchRegExp match toHaveMembers have members toIncludeMembers include members toHavePropertyPath have property toBeAbove above / greater than toBeBelow below / less than toHaveType have type toSatisfy satisfy toBeClickable clickable state (locator) Then('I expect {locator} to be ready', async function (this: QavajsPlaywrightWorld, locator: Locator) { await this.expect(locator).toBeClickable(); await this.expect(await locator.textContent()).toInclude('Ready'); }); Window switching, file existence and scroll until visible waits use the same matchers: a single report step and the actual state in the error message.

Import the library after the corresponding driver library in your qavajs config: export default { require: [ 'node_modules/@qavajs/steps-playwright/index.js', // or steps-wdio 'node_modules/@qavajs/steps-accessibility-ea/index.js' ], format: [ ['@qavajs/html-formatter', 'report.html'] ], }

Runs an accessibility audit on the full page and fails if any issues at or above the configured failLevels are found. Attaches the report to the test output. When I open 'https://example.com/' url And I perform accessibility check

Accepts a JSON options object to override accessibility-checker configuration for this step only. Property Type Description context string CSS selector to scope the audit to a specific element outputFormat string[] Report formats to generate (html, json, csv, xlsx, disable) failLevels string[] Issue levels that cause the step to fail reportLevels string[] Issue levels included in the report When I open 'https://example.com/' url And I perform accessibility check: """ { "context": "[aria-label='main navigation']", "outputFormat": ["html", "json"], "failLevels": ["violation"], "reportLevels": ["violation", "potentialviolation", "recommendation"] } """

Stores the full report object in a memory variable for custom assertions. Does not throw on failures. When I open 'https://example.com/' url And I perform accessibility check and save results as 'report' Then I expect '$report.summary.counts.violation' to equal '0' With options: When I open 'https://example.com/' url And I perform accessibility check and save results as 'report': """ { "outputFormat": ["html", "json"], "failLevels": [] } """ Then I expect '$report.summary.counts.violation' to equal '0'

Playwright steps provide a couple of additional configuration properties Name Type Description Default browser object object describing playwright config (driver can be used as alias) {} pageObject object instance of page object definitions (page object) {} import App from './page_object'; export default { require: [ 'node_modules/@qavajs/steps-playwright/index.js' ], browser: { timeout: { action: 10000, // playwright action timeout present: 10000, visible: 20000, page: 10000, networkIdle: 500, // network inactivity period for 'I wait for network idle' step value: 5000, // expect value timeout valueInterval: 500, // expect value interval actionInterval: 1000, // interval to repeat action for 'I click ... until ...' steps pageRefreshInterval: 2000 // refresh page for 'I refresh page...' steps }, capabilities: { browserName: 'chromium' } }, pageObject: new App() }

To connect to playwright server, pass wsEndpoint property in the capabilities object export default { browser: { capabilities: { browserName: 'chromium', wsEndpoint: 'ws://127.0.0.1:60291/2bd48ce272de2b543e4c8c533f664b83' } }, }
To connect to the CDP endpoint, pass cdpEndpoint property in the capabilities object export default { browser: { capabilities: { browserName: 'chromium', cdpEndpoint: 'http://localhost:9222/' } } }

@qavajs/steps-playwright can also take a screenshot on a particular event. onFail beforeStep afterStep export default { browser: { screenshot: { event: ['onFail'], //event to take a screenshot fullPage: true // option to take full page screenshot (default false) } } }

@qavajs supports capturing playwright traces. https://playwright.dev/docs/next/trace-viewer-intro Supported events: onFail afterScenario export default { //... browser: { trace: { event: ['onFail'], // Events to save trace. Possible value onFail or afterScenario dir: 'dirToStoreTraces', // Dir to store traces. Default - traces/ attach: true, // Whether trace needs to be attached to the cucumber report. Default - false screenshots: true, // Whether to capture screenshots during tracing. Screenshots are used to build a timeline preview. Default - true snapshots: true, // Whether to capture DOM and network activity } } }

@qavajs supports video recording https://playwright.dev/docs/next/videos Supported events: onFail afterScenario export default { //... browser: { video: { event: ['onFail'], // Events to save video. Possible value onFail or afterScenario dir: 'video', // Dir to store video. Default is video/ size: {width: 640, height: 480}, // Video resolution attach: true // Define if video need to be attached to cucumber report. Default false } } }
reuseSession flag allows to share driver session between tests. Browser will not be closed automatically after test. export default { browser: { reuseSession: true } }
restartBrowser flag allows to restart browser between tests instead of default restarting context export default { browser: { restartBrowser: true } }

npm install @qavajs/steps-wdio Requires Node.js 22.19.0 or later and WebdriverIO v10 (use @qavajs/steps-wdio@2 for WebdriverIO v9).

@qavajs/steps-wdio@3 is built on WebdriverIO v10. Gherkin steps are unchanged, but some WebdriverIO behavior changed underneath them: Change What to do Node.js 22.19.0+ is required Upgrade Node.js WebDriver BiDi is the default protocol Nothing for built-in steps: frame and window steps work in both BiDi and Classic sessions. Set 'wdio:enforceWebDriverClassic': true in capabilities to keep using Classic Single element lookup is strict: $ throws StrictSelectorError if a selector matches more than one element Make locators unique, or set strictSelectors: false in the browser section to use the first match as before touchPerform is removed I perform touch action steps now run as W3C touch actions; same data table format browser.switchFrame / browser.switchWindow throw in BiDi sessions In custom steps use this.wdio.switchFrame / this.wdio.switchWindow (see Context properties) getCookies('name') / getCookies(['name']) are rejected In custom steps pass an object filter: getCookies({ name: 'name' }) Appium 3 is required; capabilities need the appium: prefix (appium:deviceName, appium:automationName) Update Appium and capabilities See the WebdriverIO v10 migration guide for the full list of changes that may affect custom steps.

wdio steps provide additional configuration properties Name Type Description Default browser object object describing wdio config (driver can be used as alias) {} pageObject object instance of page object definitions (page object) {} import App from './page_object'; export default { require: [ 'node_modules/@qavajs/steps-wdio/index.js' ], browser: { timeout: { present: 10000, visible: 20000, clickable: 15000, page: 10000, implicit: 0, //wdio implicit wait for element, element: 2000,//timeout to element to be accessible, value: 5000, // expect value timeout valueInterval: 500, //expect value interval actionInterval: 1000, // interval to repeat action for 'I click ... until ...' steps pageRefreshInterval: 2000 // interval to refresh page for 'I refresh page until ...' steps }, capabilities: { browserName: 'chrome' } }, pageObject: new App() } Strict selectors Since WebdriverIO v10 resolving a single element throws StrictSelectorError if the selector matches more than one element. Set strictSelectors: false in the browser section to restore the v9 behavior (first matched element is used).

The qavajs is a modular test automation framework designed to minimize setup time and streamline the development of test scripts. It incorporates the best test automation tools and practices into a single whole. The framework achieves efficiency through its built-in page object engine and ready-to-use sets of domain-agnostic step definitions suitable for both API and UI testing of the web and native mobile applications. Additionally, qavajs provides out of the box integration with ReportPortal, Mobitru, and the Xray and many more. Next, you will be shown how to build your own low-code test automation framework with the qavajs.

Once you have set up a clear Node.js (>=20) project, run the command npm init @qavajs to launch the CLI application. This will configure qavajs and install the necessary modules for your testing purposes. After the process is completed, a config.ts (or config.js) file will be generated in the project's root directory, which will be used to configure test execution.

As the qavajs based on the Cucumber the test scripts are written in Gherkin language of both built-in steps and those you will create yourself. With years of experience across various domains, we have implemented numerous packages of step definitions that you can utilize. Feature: Wikipedia @wikipedia Scenario Outline: Search in wikipedia (<term>) Given I open '$wikipediaUrl' url When I type '<term>' to 'Wikipedia > Search Input' And I click 'Wikipedia > Search Button' And I expect text of 'Wikipedia Article > Title' equals '<term>' And I expect text of 'Wikipedia Article > Title' not to contain 'Python' And I expect 'Wikipedia Article > Title' to be visible Examples: | term | | JavaScript | | Java | It is worth mentioning the expression '$wikipediaUrl' in the example above, starting with '$' interpreted as a qavajs memory variable whose value is taken from the Memory class instance in runtime. More details. Another feature is a locator alias expression like 'Wikipedia > Search Input' separated by the '>' sign that describes hierarchical page structure. See how to organize your page object.
In addition to the default features of Cucumber config file, the qavajs config implements the following capabilities to provide advanced flexibility.

If you have the basic config npx qavajs will launch test execution. To specify a custom path to the config file, use npx qavajs run --config <config> In case your config exports an object with multiple properties, you can specify which property to read npx qavajs run --profile <profile> If --config is omitted, config.ts, config.js, config.mjs or config.cjs from the current directory is used. Feature files can be passed as positional arguments (with optional line numbers); they are added to --paths: npx qavajs run features/login.feature:12 features/cart.feature Run npx qavajs --help to see all options and npx qavajs --version to print the installed version. Before the run qavajs prints a table with the resolved configuration (use --quiet to hide it). The table is printed without colors when output is not a terminal or NO_COLOR is set (FORCE_COLOR overrides this). CLI options​ Flag Type Description --config string Config file path --profile string Profile name to run --paths string[] Paths to feature files --tags, -t string[] Tag expression filter (multiple flags are ANDed) --format, -f string[] Formatter name/path and optional output file --format-options string[] JSON options for formatters (merged) --import, -i string[] Support code paths (ESM) --require, -r string[] Support code paths (CJS) --require-module string[] Transpilation modules to load via require() --name string[] Scenario name regex filters --order string Run order (defined or random) --parallel number Number of worker processes --retry number Retry failing tests N times --retry-tag-filter string[] Tag expression for retryable scenarios --dry-run, -d boolean Prepare run without executing --backtrace, -b boolean Show full error backtraces --fail-fast boolean Stop on first failure --force-exit boolean Call process.exit() after run --strict boolean Fail on pending steps --shard string Shard tests (x/y) --world-parameters string[] JSON parameters passed to World (merged) --memory-values string JSON values to override in memory --no-error-exit boolean Suppress non-zero exit code on test failure --quiet, -q boolean Do not print the config table --help, -h boolean Show help --version, -v boolean Show version --format-options and --world-parameters can be passed multiple times; the JSON objects are merged. Unknown options are not rejected (they can be read by your code via CLI_ARGV), but options that look like a typo of a known one (e.g. --tag) produce a warning. Invalid values (malformed JSON in --world-parameters/--format-options/--memory-values, non-integer --parallel/--retry, unknown profile or missing config file) fail fast with a readable error.

UI mode opens an interactive test runner in the browser: npx qavajs ui --config <config> --profile <profile> browse features, rules, scenario outlines and examples as a tree with live status run all tests, a feature, a rule, an outline or a single scenario; stop a run at any time filter by name, file or @tag, and by status (failed, passed, skipped, not run) inspect steps with durations, errors, data tables, doc strings and attachments (logs, images, video, json) view the feature source with step results, and the full console output of the run reload the test tree after changing features or step definitions Every run is executed in a separate process with the same config, profile and CLI options (--tags, --world-parameters, --memory-values, etc.), so BeforeExecution/AfterExecution hooks are called once per run. Formatters from the config are not used in UI mode. Flag Default Description --port random Port of the UI server --host localhost Host to bind the UI server to --no-open Do not open the browser automatically Keyboard shortcuts: F5 / Ctrl+Enter run visible tests, Esc stops the run, / focuses the filter, arrow keys navigate the tree, Enter runs the focused item.
Page object guide

In case tests need to be run with an updated memory value, they can be passed via CLI (e.g, run scenarios on some other URL) It can be done by passing --memory-values parameter, which is JSON with params that need to be overridden. For instance, to override the $url value: npx qavajs run --config config.ts --memory-values '{"url": "https://github.com"}'
All params that you passed to the qavajs CLI will be available in the CLI_ARGV environment variable in all child workers.

The value parameter type provides an API to access memory When('Read memory {value}', async function(memoryValue) { expect(await memoryValue.value()).to.equal('ts'); }); When('Set memory {value} as {string}', async function(memoryKey, value) { memoryKey.set(value); });

validation parameter type provides an API to verify values by a certain condition When('I expect {string} {validation} {string}', async function(value1, validate, value2) { validate(value1, value2); });

You can use the softly prefix before expect to continue test execution after an error. Feature: Feature Scenario: verify soft assert # first step fails, but other steps will not be skipped Then I expect '2' to softly equal '1' # pass And I expect '1' to softly equal '1' # fail And I expect '2' to softly equal '1' # skip And I expect '1' to softly equal '1'

qavajs supports cucumber-js built-in sharding to split your tests between different machines. To do so pass --shard x/y parameter in CLI, where x - current shard, y - total number of shards. npx qavajs run --config config.js --shard 1/2 npx qavajs run --config config.js --shard 2/2

It is possible to implement complex logic using built-in qavajs steps via executeStep world method When('I do smth complex', async function() { await this.executeStep(`I type 'username' to 'Username Input'`); await this.executeStep(`I type 'password' to 'Password Input'`); await this.executeStep(`I click 'Login Button'`); await this.executeStep(`I fill following fields`, new DataTable([ [ 'Order', '123' ], [ 'Delivery Location', 'New York' ] ])) });
Also, it is possible to call other test cases via executeTest world method When('I do smth complex', async function() { await this.executeTest('feature/Login.feature', 'Login'); });

Module extends the CucumberJS world with additional entities entity type description example config object loaded config this.config.parallel executeStep function programmatically execute certain step definition await this.executeStep("I type 'username' to 'Username Input'"); setValue function set memory value await this.setValue('key', 'value'); getValue function get memory value or expression await this.getValue('$key'); validation function get validation function based await this.getValue('to equal');

Override function provides the capability to override step implementation and avoid ambiguous exceptions import { Override } from '@qavajs/core'; When('I do test', async function () {}); Override('I do test', async function () { console.log('I am overridden'); });

Fixture provides a convenient way to prepare a test environment for a specific test. This example will open the PDP page before the test and clean the cart after the test import { Fixture } from '@qavajs/core'; Fixture({ name: 'pdp', tags: '@pdp' }, async function() { await this.playwright.page.goto('https://my-site/pdp'); // fixture may return function that will be executed after test return async function() { await this.playwright.page.request.get('/cleanCart'); } }); Feature: feature with fixture @pdp Scenario: scenario with fixture When I click 'qavajs T-shirt' And I click 'cart icon' Then I expect 'qavajs T-shirt cart item' to be visible

Template provides a way to define step definitions using Gherkin language import { When, Template } from '@qavajs/core'; When('I click {string} and verify {string}', Template((locator, expected) => ` I click '${locator}' I expect '${locator} > Value' to equal '${expected}' `));

BeforeExecution and AfterExecution allow us to define hooks that will be executed once before/after whole test execution import { BeforeExecution, AfterExecution } from '@qavajs/core'; import { Server } from './server'; const server = new Server(); BeforeExecution(async function () { await server.start(); }); AfterExecution(async function () { await server.stop(); });
